title.narrative: NIHR Development Awards Call 1: Co-developing a digitally integrated care pathway for maternity care

description.narrative:
A low- and middle-income country (LMIC) award led by the University of Colombo, Sri Lanka, with mentorship from the University of Birmingham, UK, which aims to reduce long-term complications and improve clinical outcomes and quality of life for pregnant women in Sri Lanka.
Due to commence in January 2025, the one-year award intends to manage hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, improve Sri Lanka’s maternal care information system for future research and assist health professionals in decision-making.
Sri Lanka is a low-middle-income country. Despite vast improvements in reducing the number of women dying during or soon after delivery in the country, quality of care and reducing complications and the development of pregnancy-related conditions is still an ongoing issue. Specifically, the award aims to form a diverse stakeholder group to provide comprehensive expertise throughout the project’s lifecycle and beyond, as well as co-creating a prototype of a digital Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) embedded within Sri Lanka’s Electronic Health Records (EHR) system with an initial focus on hypertensive disorders during pregnancy. Plans to generate a co-developed research proposal for funding to test and evaluate the EHR and CDSS system are also highlighted. These research activities provide an opportunity to improve in-country information systems in maternal care for future research, health system strengthening and eventually in establishing a learning health system.

This award has three objectives:
1. To establish an inclusive and representative stakeholder consultation group to provide comprehensive expertise throughout the project's lifecycle and beyond. 2. To co-develop a comprehensive maternity Electronic Health Record and clinical decision support system prototype for managing hypertensive disorders during antenatal care. 3. To co-develop an applied global health research proposal to improve antenatal care during pregnancy in Sri Lanka, and test and evaluate the prototype in antenatal hospital clinics.
